idiom_name: struct security_ctx threaded as an explicit pointer parameter
implementation_notes: C has no ambient scope, so the classic container becomes a struct security_ctx passed explicitly along the call chain - the convention C APIs already use for their state (lua_State, sqlite3, a FILE *) - and each guard rejects a NULL or empty context instead of looking up a holder. This is the safest realization: lifetimes are visible in every signature, nothing survives the call, and there is no thread association to get wrong. The hand-threaded form is the only option when the identity must reach a callback whose signature you cannot change; for that case use the thread-local variant.
pitfalls: NULL must mean unauthenticated, not "system": a guard that treats a missing context as privileged turns the pattern into a bypass.
Every new call path must pass the pointer; the compiler will not notice a path that silently passes a context built from an unauthenticated request.
The context must outlive the call: returning a pointer to a stack-allocated context is undefined behaviour.

variants.name: Thread storage duration / POSIX TSD (C11)
variants.implementation_notes: When the guard sits too deep to thread a parameter, the only language-level carriers are C11 thread storage duration (_Thread_local, spelled thread_local through <threads.h>) and POSIX thread-specific data (pthread_key_create/pthread_setspecific/pthread_getspecific), which the man page describes as a per-thread void * area indexed by keys. Both are per-thread only: they do not cross pthread_create boundaries, they are not inherited, and they offer no lifecycle help, so the request boundary must set and clear them itself. Use this only for legacy callback signatures or C libraries that cannot receive a context pointer.
pitfalls: A thread-local context must be cleared on every exit path (pthread_setspecific(key, NULL)) before the thread returns to a pool, or the next request inherits the previous principal.
_Thread_local requires C11 and is not shared with threads you create: worker threads must be handed the context explicitly.
pthread_getspecific returns NULL both for "no key" and "no value", so guard against confusing an unset key with an unauthenticated caller.
